candidates.name: propose_agent_template
candidates.description: Propose a new or updated Twig template for user approval. Validates the template and runs a sandboxed test-render; if both pass, stores the payload server-side and returns a proposalId. Nothing is written to disk until a human approves the proposal in Studio. Use action=create for new templates, action=update to replace an existing one. The review widget is shown to the user automatically once the proposal succeeds; end your turn after a successful proposal. contextDocumentId (optional, integer) — when set, the proposal widget links to this document via Open / Refresh buttons and the resolver re-checks it at approve time. reassignDocument (optional, boolean) — when true (with contextDocumentId), the resolver also reassigns the document's template field to this slug on approve. Use for clone-and-reassign refinement of a non-agent template.

action.description: Operation: "create" for a new template, "update" to replace an existing one.

type.description: Template type: "page", "snippet", or "partial".

slug.description: Unique slug identifier for the template (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, underscores).

label.description: Human-readable label shown in the Studio template dropdown.

main.description: Complete Twig source for the template file.

description.description: Optional description of the template's purpose.

contextDocumentId.description: Optional document this proposal is about. The widget will offer "Open document" / refresh on approve. For update: doc.template MUST already equal the proposed slug. For create without reassign: same. For create WITH reassignDocument=true: doc.template MUST NOT equal the slug (clone-and-reassign path). Rejected for partial templates.

reassignDocument.description: When true (and contextDocumentId is set), on approve the resolver also setTemplate() on the doc to point at this slug. Used for clone-and-reassign refinement when the doc was on a project (non-agent) template. Defaults to false.

candidates.name: propose_document_update
candidates.description: Propose changes to one or more Pimcore documents for user approval. Does NOT write — stores the validated payload server-side and returns a proposalId per document; the user reviews each proposal in a chat-side modal and approves or rejects. The review widget is shown to the user automatically once a proposal succeeds; end your turn after a successful proposal. Use for non-trivial / visible / multi-section changes; use update_document for small explicitly-authorized edits. See the document-editing skill for editable naming, areablock/block composition, and target-group (personalization) rules — all required reading before calling.

proposals.description: Array of proposals. Each entry: {"id": <documentId>, "data": {<update_document data>}, "targetGroupId": <int, optional>}. The "data" shape is identical to update_document's data argument: {"editables": {...}, "settings": {...}, "properties": {...}, "appendEditables": <bool>}. When "targetGroupId" is set, only "editables" is allowed in "data". Max 20 entries per call. Pass the array directly — a JSON-encoded string is rejected. wysiwyg/HTML values with embedded quotes are the #1 cause of parse errors when the array is re-stringified.

id.description: Single-document shortcut: document id. Use only when proposing changes for ONE document — the tool auto-wraps {id, data?, editables?, settings?, properties?} into a one-element proposals array. Ignored when `proposals` is provided.

data.description: Single-document shortcut: full data envelope ({editables?, settings?, properties?, appendEditables?}).

targetGroupId.description: Single-document shortcut: personalization target-group id (from list_target_groups). When set, editables are written as group-specific variants; `appendEditables` is forced to true; `settings` and `properties` must be empty. Applies ONLY to the single-document shortcut (paired with `id`). Ignored when `proposals` is provided — use per-entry `targetGroupId` in that case.

summary.description: Optional one-line caption shown above the proposal review widget (1-3 sentences). When omitted, a neutral caption is generated automatically.

candidates.name: get_document_schema
candidates.description: Return the editable schema of one Pimcore document: editables[], structural[] (areablocks/blocks with availableBricks palette), branches[]. See `document-editing` skill for naming conventions, write payload shapes, and per-type examples.

candidates.name: update_document
candidates.description: Update editables, settings, and/or properties on an existing document. Editable values can be passed in bare form (just the data — type inferred from the document or template schema) or wrapped form ({"type": "...", "data": ...}). Partial updates preserve other editables (appendEditables defaults to true). Pre-flights validation; on validation failure no save happens. After successful save, post-renders the document and returns any frontend errors in `renderErrors[]` — if non-empty, the document was saved BUT renders broken; pick different element ids/values and call update_document again to fix.For schema and current state, call get_document_schema and get_document first.

data.description: Object with optional keys: editables, settings, properties, appendEditables. Example: {"editables": {"headline": "New title", "cImage_3": {"id": 341}}, "settings": {"published": true}, "properties": {"navigation_color": {"type": "text", "data": "blue"}}}. Pass the object directly — a JSON-encoded string is rejected. wysiwyg/HTML values with embedded quotes are the #1 cause of parse errors when the object is re-stringified.

targetGroupId.description: Optional. Personalization target-group id (from list_target_groups). When set, editables are written as group-specific variants; `appendEditables` is forced to true; `settings` and `properties` must be empty in the data payload.

pqlFilter.description: PQL filter for documents. Common fields: id, type, key, fullPath, published. LIKE wildcards are `*` and `?` — NOT SQL `%` / `_`. Examples: type = "page"; key LIKE "*home*"; published = true

parentId.description: Parent folder ID to scope the search. Omit for global search.

candidates.name: get_document
candidates.description: Get one or more Pimcore documents. By default returns only the document spine (id, type, key, path, parentId, modificationDate, published) — opt in to `includeContent`, `includeSettings`, and `includeProperties` selectively to keep responses small. For SCHEMA (what edits are possible) use get_document_schema; this tool returns CURRENT state. Pass `targetGroupId` to read content for one personalization target group. See the document-editing skill for response shape, when to opt in, and the target-group workflow.

ids.description: Batch parameter — always `ids` (array), never `id`. Document IDs. Example: [12, 18]. Max 5 per call — document content can be large; batch conservatively. A JSON-encoded string like "[12, 18]" is also accepted.

includeContent.description: Include the document content (the editable widgets and their current values, areablock entries, blocks, inline-resolved element references). Default false. Opt in when reading or editing content; skip when you only need the spine.

includeSettings.description: Include document settings (title, description, controller, template, prettyUrl). Default false. Opt in when changing those.

includeProperties.description: Include document properties. Default false. Opt in when reading or editing properties.

targetGroupId.description: Optional. Personalization target-group id (from list_target_groups). When set, content is returned for that target group context (existing variants surfaced; missing ones fall back to base with `inherited: true`). Implies `includeContent: true`.

candidates.description: Propose changes to one or more data objects for user approval. Does NOT write — generates diffs for review. Returns {results: [...]} where each success entry has a proposalId and failures carry an error with retryable flag. For retryable errors, fix the data and call again with only the failed entries. The review widget is shown to the user automatically once a proposal succeeds; end your turn after a successful proposal.

proposals.description: Array of proposals. Each entry: {"id": <objectId>, "data": {<field changes>}}. Only include fields you want to change. Discover the exact shape per class via get_class_definition (top-level fields and their editableDataFormat) and get_field_schema (objectbricks, classificationstore groups, fieldcollection children). IMPORTANT: values inside `data` are LITERAL JSON. Arrays and objects are written directly — never wrap them in an extra string. Example covering the three highest-confusion shapes (placeholders in <angle brackets> — substitute real names from get_class_definition / get_field_schema): [{"id": 42, "data": {"localizedfields": {"<localizedField>": {"en": "…", "de": "…"}}, "<relationField>": [{"id": 7}], "<fcField>": [{"type": "<FCClass>", "data": {"localizedfields": {"<fcSubField>": {"en": "…"}}}}]}}]. Note: localizedfields nests as {"<fieldName>": {"<locale>": <value>}}, NOT {"<locale>": {"<fieldName>": <value>}}. Pass the array directly — a JSON-encoded string is rejected. Each entry MAY also include `removeProposedFields: ["<dotpath>", ...]` — fields to DROP from the proposal entirely (applied after merge with prior pending/refined proposals). Dot-paths work for nested keys (e.g. "localizedfields.title.en"). CRITICAL on refinement: "do not change X" / "leave X as-is" requires X in `removeProposedFields` — omitting from `data` keeps the prior proposal's value, not the persisted value.

removeProposedFields.description: Single-object shortcut: list of dot-paths to DROP from the proposal entirely (e.g. ["localizedfields.title.en", "locationAddress"]). Pair with `id`. Removes the field from the proposal — it will NOT be touched on the object. Different from sending `""`/`null`/`[]` as a value, which proposes to CLEAR the value. candidates.name: propose_data_object_update
candidates.description: Propose changes to one or more data objects for user approval. Does NOT write — generates diffs for review. Returns {results: [...]} where each success entry has a proposalId and failures carry an error with retryable flag. For retryable errors, fix the data and call again with only the failed entries. For non-retryable errors, report to the user. Use get_data_object with format="edit" first. The review widget is shown to the user automatically once a proposal succeeds; end your turn after a successful proposal.

proposals.description: Array of proposals. Each entry: {"id": <objectId>, "data": {<field changes>}}. Only include fields you want to change. Discover the exact shape per class via get_class_definition (top-level fields and their editableDataFormat) and get_field_schema (objectbricks, classificationstore groups, fieldcollection children). IMPORTANT: values inside `data` are LITERAL JSON. Arrays and objects are written directly — never wrap them in an extra string. Example covering the three highest-confusion shapes (placeholders in <angle brackets> — substitute real names from get_class_definition / get_field_schema): [{"id": 42, "data": {"localizedfields": {"<localizedField>": {"en": "…", "de": "…"}}, "<relationField>": [{"id": 7}], "<fcField>": [{"type": "<FCClass>", "data": {"localizedfields": {"<fcSubField>": {"en": "…"}}}}]}}]. Note: localizedfields nests as {"<fieldName>": {"<locale>": <value>}}, NOT {"<locale>": {"<fieldName>": <value>}}. Pass the array directly — a JSON-encoded string is rejected. Each entry MAY also include `removeProposedFields: ["<dotpath>", ...]` — fields to DROP from the proposal entirely (applied after merge with prior pending/refined proposals). Dot-paths work for nested keys (e.g. "localizedfields.title.en"). CRITICAL on refinement: "do not change X" / "leave X as-is" requires X in `removeProposedFields` — omitting from `data` keeps the prior proposal's value, not the persisted value.

removeProposedFields.description: Single-object shortcut: list of dot-paths to DROP from the proposal entirely (e.g. ["localizedfields.title.en", "locationAddress"]). Pair with `id`. By default returns only the document spine (id, type, key, path, parentId, modificationDate, published) — opt in to `includeContent`, `includeSettings`, and `includeProperties` selectively to keep responses small. For SCHEMA (what edits are possible) use get_document_schema; this tool returns CURRENT state. Pass `targetGroupId` to read content for one personalization target group. See the document-editing skill for response shape, when to opt in, and the target-group workflow.

ids.description: Batch parameter — always `ids` (array), never `id`. Document IDs. Example: [12, 18]. Max 5 per call — document content can be large; batch conservatively. A JSON-encoded string like "[12, 18]" is also accepted.

includeContent.description: Include the document content (the editable widgets and their current values, areablock entries, blocks, inline-resolved element references). Default false. Opt in when reading or editing content; skip when you only need the spine.

includeSettings.description: Include document settings (title, description, controller, template, prettyUrl). Default false. Opt in when changing those.

includeProperties.description: Include document properties. Default false. Opt in when reading or editing properties.

targetGroupId.description: Optional. Personalization target-group id (from list_target_groups). When set, content is returned for that target group context (existing variants surfaced; missing ones fall back to base with `inherited: true`). Implies `includeContent: true`.

candidates.name: list_document_types
candidates.description: List the Pimcore Document Types (presets) configured for this project. Each preset bundles a controller + template so newly-created pages render real content from the start.

candidates.name: list_editables
candidates.description: Return the sorted list of Pimcore document editable type names available in this project (e.g. input, textarea, wysiwyg, image, link, areablock, block, select, …). Call this before generating a Twig template so you know which pimcore_* Twig functions are safe to use. Returns: { editableTypes: string[] }.

candidates.name: update_document
candidates.description: Update editables, settings, and/or properties on an existing document. Editable values can be passed in bare form (just the data — type inferred from the document or template schema) or wrapped form ({"type": "...", "data": ...}). Partial updates preserve other editables (appendEditables defaults to true). Pre-flights validation; on validation failure no save happens. After successful save, post-renders the document and returns any frontend errors in `renderErrors[]` — if non-empty, the document was saved BUT renders broken; pick different element ids/values and call update_document again to fix.For schema and current state, call get_document_schema and get_document first.

data.description: Object with optional keys: editables, settings, properties, appendEditables. Example: {"editables": {"headline": "New title", "cImage_3": {"id": 341}}, "settings": {"published": true}, "properties": {"navigation_color": {"type": "text", "data": "blue"}}}. Pass the object directly — a JSON-encoded string is rejected. wysiwyg/HTML values with embedded quotes are the #1 cause of parse errors when the object is re-stringified.

targetGroupId.description: Optional. Personalization target-group id (from list_target_groups). When set, editables are written as group-specific variants; `appendEditables` is forced to true; `settings` and `properties` must be empty in the data payload.

candidates.name: propose_document_update
candidates.description: Propose changes to one or more Pimcore documents for user approval. Does NOT write — stores the validated payload server-side and returns a proposalId per document; the user reviews each proposal in a chat-side modal and approves or rejects. The review widget is shown to the user automatically once a proposal succeeds; end your turn after a successful proposal. Use for non-trivial / visible / multi-section changes; use update_document for small explicitly-authorized edits. See the document-editing skill for editable naming, areablock/block composition, and target-group (personalization) rules — all required reading before calling.

proposals.description: Array of proposals. Each entry: {"id": <documentId>, "data": {<update_document data>}, "targetGroupId": <int, optional>}. The "data" shape is identical to update_document's data argument: {"editables": {...}, "settings": {...}, "properties": {...}, "appendEditables": <bool>}. When "targetGroupId" is set, only "editables" is allowed in "data". Max 20 entries per call. Pass the array directly — a JSON-encoded string is rejected. wysiwyg/HTML values with embedded quotes are the #1 cause of parse errors when the array is re-stringified.

id.description: Single-document shortcut: document id. Use only when proposing changes for ONE document — the tool auto-wraps {id, data?, editables?, settings?, properties?} into a one-element proposals array. Ignored when `proposals` is provided.

data.description: Single-document shortcut: full data envelope ({editables?, settings?, properties?, appendEditables?}).

targetGroupId.description: Single-document shortcut: personalization target-group id (from list_target_groups). When set, editables are written as group-specific variants; `appendEditables` is forced to true; `settings` and `properties` must be empty. Applies ONLY to the single-document shortcut (paired with `id`). Ignored when `proposals` is provided — use per-entry `targetGroupId` in that case.

summary.description: Optional one-line caption shown above the proposal review widget (1-3 sentences). When omitted, a neutral caption is generated automatically.

For classification stores, use groupId to get keys for a specific group.

groupId.description: For classification store fields: get keys for this group ID.

candidates.name: propose_data_object_update
candidates.description: Propose changes to one or more data objects for user approval. Does NOT write — generates diffs for review. Returns {results: [...]} where each success entry has a proposalId and failures carry an error with retryable flag. For retryable errors, fix the data and call again with only the failed entries. For non-retryable errors, report to the user. Use get_data_object with format="edit" first. The review widget is shown to the user automatically once a proposal succeeds; end your turn after a successful proposal.

proposals.description: Array of proposals. Each entry: {"id": <objectId>, "data": {<field changes>}}. Only include fields you want to change. Discover the exact shape per class via get_class_definition (top-level fields and their editableDataFormat) and get_field_schema (objectbricks, classificationstore groups, fieldcollection children). IMPORTANT: values inside `data` are LITERAL JSON. Arrays and objects are written directly — never wrap them in an extra string. Example covering the three highest-confusion shapes (placeholders in <angle brackets> — substitute real names from get_class_definition / get_field_schema): [{"id": 42, "data": {"localizedfields": {"<localizedField>": {"en": "…", "de": "…"}}, "<relationField>": [{"id": 7}], "<fcField>": [{"type": "<FCClass>", "data": {"localizedfields": {"<fcSubField>": {"en": "…"}}}}]}}]. Note: localizedfields nests as {"<fieldName>": {"<locale>": <value>}}, NOT {"<locale>": {"<fieldName>": <value>}}. Pass the array directly — a JSON-encoded string is rejected. Each entry MAY also include `removeProposedFields: ["<dotpath>", ...]` — fields to DROP from the proposal entirely (applied after merge with prior pending/refined proposals). Dot-paths work for nested keys (e.g. "localizedfields.title.en"). CRITICAL on refinement: "do not change X" / "leave X as-is" requires X in `removeProposedFields` — omitting from `data` keeps the prior proposal's value, not the persisted value.

id.description: Single-object shortcut: data object id. Use only when proposing changes for ONE object — the tool auto-wraps {id, data?, removeProposedFields?} into a one-element proposals array. Ignored when `proposals` is provided.

data.description: Single-object shortcut: field-changes object (same shape as an entry's `data`). Pair with `id`. Ignored when `proposals` is provided.

removeProposedFields.description: Single-object shortcut: list of dot-paths to DROP from the proposal entirely (e.g. ["localizedfields.title.en", "locationAddress"]). Pair with `id`. Removes the field from the proposal — it will NOT be touched on the object. Different from sending `""`/`null`/`[]` as a value, which proposes to CLEAR the value. Ignored when `proposals` is provided.

summary.description: Optional one-line caption shown above the proposal review widget (1-3 sentences). When omitted, a neutral caption is generated automatically.

query.description: Fulltext search term (searches across all indexed fields). Leave empty to list all objects of a class.

className.description: Filter by class name (selects the class, e.g. "<ClassName>"). NOTE: className selects the class, not a field value — to filter by a field value (including objectType) use pqlFilter instead. Strongly recommended for focused results.

pqlFilter.description: PQL filter — use this to filter by any field value (including objectType); NOT raw SQL. Call get_queryable_fields first for field names/types. LIKE wildcards are `*` and `?` — NOT SQL `%` / `_`. Example: fieldName = "value" AND year > 2000

parentId.description: Parent folder ID to scope the search. Omit for global search.

extended.description: When true, each hit includes key, className, path, published, modificationDate in addition to id. Default false (ids only) — fetch details via get_data_object.

candidates.name: get_data_object
candidates.description: Get one or more data objects by ID. Default format is "preview" (compact, all languages of localized fields). Use format="edit" for the structured shape needed by propose_data_object_update. Pass fields=["name","price"] (plain names, NOT PQL paths or locale suffixes) to narrow the response. Pass languages=["en","de"] to limit localized blocks to specific locales. Use search_data_objects first to find object IDs.

ids.description: Batch parameter — always `ids` (array), never `id`. Data object IDs. Example: [42, 55, 101]. A JSON-encoded string like "[42, 55, 101]" is also accepted.

format.description: Output format: "preview" (default, compact summaries) or "edit" (structured setter-compatible data for propose_data_object_update).

fields.description: Optional. Plain field names to include, e.g. ["name","price"]. A name matches a top-level field AND any same-named child of localizedFields (one name returns every locale). Use names exactly as in get_class_definition — NOT PQL paths from get_queryable_fields (e.g. "localizedfields.en.name") and NOT locale suffixes (e.g. "name.en"); those decorated forms are coerced when unambiguous, otherwise reported in unknownFields with the valid names. Default: all fields.

languages.description: Optional. Restrict every localizedFields block to just these locales (e.g. ["en","de"]). Default: all valid languages.

candidates.name: propose_data_object_update
candidates.description: Propose changes to one or more data objects for user approval. Does NOT write — generates diffs for review. Returns {results: [...]} where each success entry has a proposalId and failures carry an error with retryable flag. For retryable errors, fix the data and call again with only the failed entries. For non-retryable errors, report to the user. Use get_data_object with format="edit" first. The review widget is shown to the user automatically once a proposal succeeds; end your turn after a successful proposal.

proposals.description: Array of proposals. Each entry: {"id": <objectId>, "data": {<field changes>}}. Only include fields you want to change. Discover the exact shape per class via get_class_definition (top-level fields and their editableDataFormat) and get_field_schema (objectbricks, classificationstore groups, fieldcollection children). IMPORTANT: values inside `data` are LITERAL JSON. Arrays and objects are written directly — never wrap them in an extra string. Example covering the three highest-confusion shapes (placeholders in <angle brackets> — substitute real names from get_class_definition / get_field_schema): [{"id": 42, "data": {"localizedfields": {"<localizedField>": {"en": "…", "de": "…"}}, "<relationField>": [{"id": 7}], "<fcField>": [{"type": "<FCClass>", "data": {"localizedfields": {"<fcSubField>": {"en": "…"}}}}]}}]. Note: localizedfields nests as {"<fieldName>": {"<locale>": <value>}}, NOT {"<locale>": {"<fieldName>": <value>}}. Pass the array directly — a JSON-encoded string is rejected. Each entry MAY also include `removeProposedFields: ["<dotpath>", ...]` — fields to DROP from the proposal entirely (applied after merge with prior pending/refined proposals). Dot-paths work for nested keys (e.g. "localizedfields.title.en"). CRITICAL on refinement: "do not change X" / "leave X as-is" requires X in `removeProposedFields` — omitting from `data` keeps the prior proposal's value, not the persisted value.

id.description: Single-object shortcut: data object id. Use only when proposing changes for ONE object — the tool auto-wraps {id, data?, removeProposedFields?} into a one-element proposals array. Ignored when `proposals` is provided.

data.description: Single-object shortcut: field-changes object (same shape as an entry's `data`). Pair with `id`. Ignored when `proposals` is provided.

removeProposedFields.description: Single-object shortcut: list of dot-paths to DROP from the proposal entirely (e.g. ["localizedfields.title.en", "locationAddress"]). Pair with `id`. Removes the field from the proposal — it will NOT be touched on the object. Different from sending `""`/`null`/`[]` as a value, which proposes to CLEAR the value. Ignored when `proposals` is provided.

summary.description: Optional one-line caption shown above the proposal review widget (1-3 sentences). When omitted, a neutral caption is generated automatically.

candidates.description: Propose custom metadata changes to one or more assets for user approval. Does NOT write — generates diffs for review. Returns {results: [...]} where each success entry has a proposalId and failures carry an error with retryable flag. The review widget is shown to the user automatically once a proposal succeeds; end your turn after a successful proposal.

proposals.description: Array of proposals — pass it directly, never as a string. Each entry: {"id": <assetId>, "metadata": [{name, language, type, data}, ...]}. Use get_asset with format="edit" first to see the exact names, types, and dataFormatHint per metadata entry — copy them verbatim. IMPORTANT: `data` values are LITERAL JSON. For relations write {"id": <int>, "type": "object"|"asset"|"document"} as a literal object, never a JSON-encoded string. Multi-relation fields (type "manyToManyRelation") are ADDITIVE by default: send only the member(s) you want to add and existing relations are preserved (de-duplicated by id+type). To overwrite the whole list instead, set "replace": true on that metadata entry. Example (placeholders in <angle brackets>): [{"id": 42, "metadata": [{"name": "<metadataName>", "language": "", "type": "input", "data": "<literal string value>"}, {"name": "<relationMetadataName>", "language": "", "type": "object", "data": {"id": 7, "type": "object"}}]}].

candidates.name: update_document

Editable values can be passed in bare form (just the data — type inferred from the document or template schema) or wrapped form ({"type": "...", "data": ...}). Pass the object directly — a JSON-encoded string is rejected. wysiwyg/HTML values with embedded quotes are the #1 cause of parse errors when the object is re-stringified.

targetGroupId.description: Optional. Personalization target-group id (from list_target_groups). When set, editables are written as group-specific variants; `appendEditables` is forced to true; `settings` and `properties` must be empty in the data payload.

type.description: Document type. "page"/"snippet"/"email" have editables; "folder" organizes others; "link"/"hardlink" point elsewhere.

title.description: Page title (used as document title for SEO and navigation; only meaningful for type=page). Empty string by default.

navigationName.description: Navigation name (only meaningful for type=page; stored as a property).

template.description: Twig template (e.g. "content/default.html.twig"). Used when type=page/snippet/email. Leave empty when using docTypeId (the preset supplies the template).

docTypeId.description: docTypeId — id of a preset Document Type. When set, supplies controller+template from the preset. Mutually exclusive with explicit template/controller.

Does NOT write — stores the validated payload server-side and returns a proposalId per document; the user reviews each proposal in a chat-side modal and approves or rejects. The review widget is shown to the user automatically once a proposal succeeds; end your turn after a successful proposal. Use for non-trivial / visible / multi-section changes; use update_document for small explicitly-authorized edits. See the document-editing skill for editable naming, areablock/block composition, and target-group (personalization) rules — all required reading before calling.

proposals.description: Array of proposals. Each entry: {"id": <documentId>, "data": {<update_document data>}, "targetGroupId": <int, optional>}. The "data" shape is identical to update_document's data argument: {"editables": {...}, "settings": {...}, "properties": {...}, "appendEditables": <bool>}. When "targetGroupId" is set, only "editables" is allowed in "data". Max 20 entries per call. Pass the array directly — a JSON-encoded string is rejected. wysiwyg/HTML values with embedded quotes are the #1 cause of parse errors when the array is re-stringified.

targetGroupId.description: Single-document shortcut: personalization target-group id (from list_target_groups). When set, editables are written as group-specific variants; `appendEditables` is forced to true; `settings` and `properties` must be empty. Applies ONLY to the single-document shortcut (paired with `id`). Ignored when `proposals` is provided — use per-entry `targetGroupId` in that case.

Use format="edit" for the structured shape needed by propose_data_object_update. Pass fields=["name","price"] (plain names, NOT PQL paths or locale suffixes) to narrow the response. Use names exactly as in get_class_definition — NOT PQL paths from get_queryable_fields (e.g. "localizedfields.en.name") and NOT locale suffixes (e.g. "name.en"); those decorated forms are coerced when unambiguous, otherwise reported in unknownFields with the valid names. candidates.name: propose_data_object_update
candidates.description: Propose changes to one or more data objects for user approval. Does NOT write — generates diffs for review. Returns {results: [...]} where each success entry has a proposalId and failures carry an error with retryable flag. For retryable errors, fix the data and call again with only the failed entries. For non-retryable errors, report to the user. Use get_data_object with format="edit" first. The review widget is shown to the user automatically once a proposal succeeds; end your turn after a successful proposal.

proposals.description: Array of proposals. Each entry: {"id": <objectId>, "data": {<field changes>}}. Only include fields you want to change. Discover the exact shape per class via get_class_definition (top-level fields and their editableDataFormat) and get_field_schema (objectbricks, classificationstore groups, fieldcollection children). IMPORTANT: values inside `data` are LITERAL JSON. Arrays and objects are written directly — never wrap them in an extra string. Example covering the three highest-confusion shapes (placeholders in <angle brackets> — substitute real names from get_class_definition / get_field_schema): [{"id": 42, "data": {"localizedfields": {"<localizedField>": {"en": "…", "de": "…"}}, "<relationField>": [{"id": 7}], "<fcField>": [{"type": "<FCClass>", "data": {"localizedfields": {"<fcSubField>": {"en": "…"}}}}]}}]. Note: localizedfields nests as {"<fieldName>": {"<locale>": <value>}}, NOT {"<locale>": {"<fieldName>": <value>}}. Pass the array directly — a JSON-encoded string is rejected. Each entry MAY also include `removeProposedFields: ["<dotpath>", ...]` — fields to DROP from the proposal entirely (applied after merge with prior pending/refined proposals). Dot-paths work for nested keys (e.g. "localizedfields.title.en"). CRITICAL on refinement: "do not change X" / "leave X as-is" requires X in `removeProposedFields` — omitting from `data` keeps the prior proposal's value, not the persisted value.

id.description: Single-object shortcut: data object id. Use only when proposing changes for ONE object — the tool auto-wraps {id, data?, removeProposedFields?} into a one-element proposals array. Ignored when `proposals` is provided.

data.description: Single-object shortcut: field-changes object (same shape as an entry's `data`). Pair with `id`. Ignored when `proposals` is provided.

removeProposedFields.description: Single-object shortcut: list of dot-paths to DROP from the proposal entirely (e.g. ["localizedfields.title.en", "locationAddress"]). Pair with `id`. Removes the field from the proposal — it will NOT be touched on the object. Different from sending `""`/`null`/`[]` as a value, which proposes to CLEAR the value. Ignored when `proposals` is provided.

removeProposedFields.description: Single-object shortcut: list of dot-paths to DROP from the proposal entirely (e.g. ["localizedfields.title.en", "locationAddress"]). Pair with `id`. candidates.name: update_document
candidates.description: Update editables, settings, and/or properties on an existing document. Editable values can be passed in bare form (just the data — type inferred from the document or template schema) or wrapped form ({"type": "...", "data": ...}). data.description: Object with optional keys: editables, settings, properties, appendEditables. Pass the object directly — a JSON-encoded string is rejected. wysiwyg/HTML values with embedded quotes are the #1 cause of parse errors when the object is re-stringified.

targetGroupId.description: Optional. Personalization target-group id (from list_target_groups). When set, editables are written as group-specific variants; `appendEditables` is forced to true; `settings` and `properties` must be empty in the data payload.

includeProperties.description: Include document properties. Default false. Opt in when reading or editing properties.

candidates.name: propose_agent_template
candidates.description: Propose a new or updated Twig template for user approval. Validates the template and runs a sandboxed test-render; if both pass, stores the payload server-side and returns a proposalId. Nothing is written to disk until a human approves the proposal in Studio. Use action=create for new templates, action=update to replace an existing one. The review widget is shown to the user automatically once the proposal succeeds; end your turn after a successful proposal. contextDocumentId (optional, integer) — when set, the proposal widget links to this document via Open / Refresh buttons and the resolver re-checks it at approve time. reassignDocument (optional, boolean) — when true (with contextDocumentId), the resolver also reassigns the document's template field to this slug on approve. Use for clone-and-reassign refinement of a non-agent template.

action.description: Operation: "create" for a new template, "update" to replace an existing one.

type.description: Template type: "page", "snippet", or "partial".

slug.description: Unique slug identifier for the template (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, underscores).

label.description: Human-readable label shown in the Studio template dropdown.

main.description: Complete Twig source for the template file.

description.description: Optional description of the template's purpose.

contextDocumentId.description: Optional document this proposal is about. The widget will offer "Open document" / refresh on approve. For update: doc.template MUST already equal the proposed slug. For create without reassign: same. For create WITH reassignDocument=true: doc.template MUST NOT equal the slug (clone-and-reassign path). Rejected for partial templates.

reassignDocument.description: When true (and contextDocumentId is set), on approve the resolver also setTemplate() on the doc to point at this slug. Used for clone-and-reassign refinement when the doc was on a project (non-agent) template. Defaults to false.

candidates.name: update_document
candidates.description: Update editables, settings, and/or properties on an existing document. Editable values can be passed in bare form (just the data — type inferred from the document or template schema) or wrapped form ({"type": "...", "data": ...}). Partial updates preserve other editables (appendEditables defaults to true). Pre-flights validation; on validation failure no save happens. After successful save, post-renders the document and returns any frontend errors in `renderErrors[]` — if non-empty, the document was saved BUT renders broken; pick different element ids/values and call update_document again to fix.For schema and current state, call get_document_schema and get_document first.

data.description: Object with optional keys: editables, settings, properties, appendEditables. Example: {"editables": {"headline": "New title", "cImage_3": {"id": 341}}, "settings": {"published": true}, "properties": {"navigation_color": {"type": "text", "data": "blue"}}}. Pass the object directly — a JSON-encoded string is rejected. wysiwyg/HTML values with embedded quotes are the #1 cause of parse errors when the object is re-stringified.

targetGroupId.description: Optional. Personalization target-group id (from list_target_groups). When set, editables are written as group-specific variants; `appendEditables` is forced to true; `settings` and `properties` must be empty in the data payload.

type.description: Document type. "page"/"snippet"/"email" have editables; "folder" organizes others; "link"/"hardlink" point elsewhere.

candidates.name: get_document
candidates.description: Get one or more Pimcore documents. By default returns only the document spine (id, type, key, path, parentId, modificationDate, published) — opt in to `includeContent`, `includeSettings`, and `includeProperties` selectively to keep responses small. For SCHEMA (what edits are possible) use get_document_schema; this tool returns CURRENT state. Pass `targetGroupId` to read content for one personalization target group. See the document-editing skill for response shape, when to opt in, and the target-group workflow.

ids.description: Batch parameter — always `ids` (array), never `id`. Document IDs. Example: [12, 18]. Max 5 per call — document content can be large; batch conservatively. A JSON-encoded string like "[12, 18]" is also accepted.

includeContent.description: Include the document content (the editable widgets and their current values, areablock entries, blocks, inline-resolved element references). Default false. Opt in when reading or editing content; skip when you only need the spine.

includeSettings.description: Include document settings (title, description, controller, template, prettyUrl). Default false. Opt in when changing those.

includeProperties.description: Include document properties. Default false. Opt in when reading or editing properties.

targetGroupId.description: Optional. Personalization target-group id (from list_target_groups). When set, content is returned for that target group context (existing variants surfaced; missing ones fall back to base with `inherited: true`). Implies `includeContent: true`.

candidates.name: propose_document_update
candidates.description: Propose changes to one or more Pimcore documents for user approval. Does NOT write — stores the validated payload server-side and returns a proposalId per document; the user reviews each proposal in a chat-side modal and approves or rejects. The review widget is shown to the user automatically once a proposal succeeds; end your turn after a successful proposal. Use for non-trivial / visible / multi-section changes; use update_document for small explicitly-authorized edits. See the document-editing skill for editable naming, areablock/block composition, and target-group (personalization) rules — all required reading before calling.

proposals.description: Array of proposals. Each entry: {"id": <documentId>, "data": {<update_document data>}, "targetGroupId": <int, optional>}. The "data" shape is identical to update_document's data argument: {"editables": {...}, "settings": {...}, "properties": {...}, "appendEditables": <bool>}. When "targetGroupId" is set, only "editables" is allowed in "data". Max 20 entries per call. Pass the array directly — a JSON-encoded string is rejected. wysiwyg/HTML values with embedded quotes are the #1 cause of parse errors when the array is re-stringified.

id.description: Single-document shortcut: document id. Use only when proposing changes for ONE document — the tool auto-wraps {id, data?, editables?, settings?, properties?} into a one-element proposals array. Ignored when `proposals` is provided.

data.description: Single-document shortcut: full data envelope ({editables?, settings?, properties?, appendEditables?}).

targetGroupId.description: Single-document shortcut: personalization target-group id (from list_target_groups). When set, editables are written as group-specific variants; `appendEditables` is forced to true; `settings` and `properties` must be empty. Applies ONLY to the single-document shortcut (paired with `id`). Ignored when `proposals` is provided — use per-entry `targetGroupId` in that case.

summary.description: Optional one-line caption shown above the proposal review widget (1-3 sentences). When omitted, a neutral caption is generated automatically.

candidates.name: get_document_schema
candidates.description: Return the editable schema of one Pimcore document: editables[], structural[] (areablocks/blocks with availableBricks palette), branches[]. See `document-editing` skill for naming conventions, write payload shapes, and per-type examples.

candidates.name: list_editables
candidates.description: Return the sorted list of Pimcore document editable type names available in this project (e.g. input, textarea, wysiwyg, image, link, areablock, block, select, …). query.description: Fulltext search term. Searches document key/title/path.

candidates.name: list_classes
candidates.description: List all available Pimcore data object classes. Returns class names, IDs, and field summaries. Use this first to discover what data types exist before searching.

candidates.name: get_data_object
candidates.description: Get one or more data objects by ID. Default format is "preview" (compact, all languages of localized fields). Use format="edit" for the structured shape needed by propose_data_object_update. Pass fields=["name","price"] (plain names, NOT PQL paths or locale suffixes) to narrow the response. Pass languages=["en","de"] to limit localized blocks to specific locales. Use search_data_objects first to find object IDs.

ids.description: Batch parameter — always `ids` (array), never `id`. Data object IDs. Example: [42, 55, 101]. A JSON-encoded string like "[42, 55, 101]" is also accepted.

format.description: Output format: "preview" (default, compact summaries) or "edit" (structured setter-compatible data for propose_data_object_update).

fields.description: Optional. Plain field names to include, e.g. ["name","price"]. A name matches a top-level field AND any same-named child of localizedFields (one name returns every locale). Use names exactly as in get_class_definition — NOT PQL paths from get_queryable_fields (e.g. "localizedfields.en.name") and NOT locale suffixes (e.g. "name.en"); those decorated forms are coerced when unambiguous, otherwise reported in unknownFields with the valid names. Default: all fields.

languages.description: Optional. Restrict every localizedFields block to just these locales (e.g. ["en","de"]). Default: all valid languages.

candidates.name: propose_data_object_update
candidates.description: Propose changes to one or more data objects for user approval. Does NOT write — generates diffs for review. Returns {results: [...]} where each success entry has a proposalId and failures carry an error with retryable flag. For retryable errors, fix the data and call again with only the failed entries. For non-retryable errors, report to the user. Use get_data_object with format="edit" first. The review widget is shown to the user automatically once a proposal succeeds; end your turn after a successful proposal.

proposals.description: Array of proposals. Each entry: {"id": <objectId>, "data": {<field changes>}}. Only include fields you want to change. Discover the exact shape per class via get_class_definition (top-level fields and their editableDataFormat) and get_field_schema (objectbricks, classificationstore groups, fieldcollection children). IMPORTANT: values inside `data` are LITERAL JSON. Arrays and objects are written directly — never wrap them in an extra string. Example covering the three highest-confusion shapes (placeholders in <angle brackets> — substitute real names from get_class_definition / get_field_schema): [{"id": 42, "data": {"localizedfields": {"<localizedField>": {"en": "…", "de": "…"}}, "<relationField>": [{"id": 7}], "<fcField>": [{"type": "<FCClass>", "data": {"localizedfields": {"<fcSubField>": {"en": "…"}}}}]}}]. Note: localizedfields nests as {"<fieldName>": {"<locale>": <value>}}, NOT {"<locale>": {"<fieldName>": <value>}}. Pass the array directly — a JSON-encoded string is rejected. Each entry MAY also include `removeProposedFields: ["<dotpath>", ...]` — fields to DROP from the proposal entirely (applied after merge with prior pending/refined proposals). Dot-paths work for nested keys (e.g. "localizedfields.title.en"). CRITICAL on refinement: "do not change X" / "leave X as-is" requires X in `removeProposedFields` — omitting from `data` keeps the prior proposal's value, not the persisted value.

id.description: Single-object shortcut: data object id. Use only when proposing changes for ONE object — the tool auto-wraps {id, data?, removeProposedFields?} into a one-element proposals array. Ignored when `proposals` is provided.

data.description: Single-object shortcut: field-changes object (same shape as an entry's `data`). Pair with `id`. Ignored when `proposals` is provided.

removeProposedFields.description: Single-object shortcut: list of dot-paths to DROP from the proposal entirely (e.g. ["localizedfields.title.en", "locationAddress"]). Pair with `id`. Removes the field from the proposal — it will NOT be touched on the object. Different from sending `""`/`null`/`[]` as a value, which proposes to CLEAR the value. Ignored when `proposals` is provided.

summary.description: Optional one-line caption shown above the proposal review widget (1-3 sentences). When omitted, a neutral caption is generated automatically.

candidates.name: propose_asset_metadata_update
candidates.description: Propose custom metadata changes to one or more assets for user approval. Does NOT write — generates diffs for review. Returns {results: [...]} where each success entry has a proposalId and failures carry an error with retryable flag. The review widget is shown to the user automatically once a proposal succeeds; end your turn after a successful proposal.

Example (placeholders in <angle brackets>): [{"id": 42, "metadata": [{"name": "<metadataName>", "language": "", "type": "input", "data": "<literal string value>"}, {"name": "<relationMetadataName>", "language": "", "type": "object", "data": {"id": 7, "type": "object"}}]}].

candidates.name: propose_data_object_update
candidates.description: Propose changes to one or more data objects for user approval. Does NOT write — generates diffs for review. Returns {results: [...]} where each success entry has a proposalId and failures carry an error with retryable flag. For retryable errors, fix the data and call again with only the failed entries. For non-retryable errors, report to the user. Use get_data_object with format="edit" first. The review widget is shown to the user automatically once a proposal succeeds; end your turn after a successful proposal.

proposals.description: Array of proposals. Each entry: {"id": <objectId>, "data": {<field changes>}}. Only include fields you want to change. Discover the exact shape per class via get_class_definition (top-level fields and their editableDataFormat) and get_field_schema (objectbricks, classificationstore groups, fieldcollection children). IMPORTANT: values inside `data` are LITERAL JSON. Arrays and objects are written directly — never wrap them in an extra string. Example covering the three highest-confusion shapes (placeholders in <angle brackets> — substitute real names from get_class_definition / get_field_schema): [{"id": 42, "data": {"localizedfields": {"<localizedField>": {"en": "…", "de": "…"}}, "<relationField>": [{"id": 7}], "<fcField>": [{"type": "<FCClass>", "data": {"localizedfields": {"<fcSubField>": {"en": "…"}}}}]}}]. Note: localizedfields nests as {"<fieldName>": {"<locale>": <value>}}, NOT {"<locale>": {"<fieldName>": <value>}}. Pass the array directly — a JSON-encoded string is rejected. Each entry MAY also include `removeProposedFields: ["<dotpath>", ...]` — fields to DROP from the proposal entirely (applied after merge with prior pending/refined proposals). Dot-paths work for nested keys (e.g. "localizedfields.title.en"). CRITICAL on refinement: "do not change X" / "leave X as-is" requires X in `removeProposedFields` — omitting from `data` keeps the prior proposal's value, not the persisted value.

id.description: Single-object shortcut: data object id. Use only when proposing changes for ONE object — the tool auto-wraps {id, data?, removeProposedFields?} into a one-element proposals array. Ignored when `proposals` is provided.

data.description: Single-object shortcut: field-changes object (same shape as an entry's `data`). Pair with `id`. Ignored when `proposals` is provided.

removeProposedFields.description: Single-object shortcut: list of dot-paths to DROP from the proposal entirely (e.g. ["localizedfields.title.en", "locationAddress"]). Pair with `id`. Removes the field from the proposal — it will NOT be touched on the object. Different from sending `""`/`null`/`[]` as a value, which proposes to CLEAR the value. Ignored when `proposals` is provided.

candidates.name: update_document
candidates.description: Update editables, settings, and/or properties on an existing document. Editable values can be passed in bare form (just the data — type inferred from the document or template schema) or wrapped form ({"type": "...", "data": ...}). Partial updates preserve other editables (appendEditables defaults to true). Pre-flights validation; on validation failure no save happens. After successful save, post-renders the document and returns any frontend errors in `renderErrors[]` — if non-empty, the document was saved BUT renders broken; pick different element ids/values and call update_document again to fix.For schema and current state, call get_document_schema and get_document first.

data.description: Object with optional keys: editables, settings, properties, appendEditables. Example: {"editables": {"headline": "New title", "cImage_3": {"id": 341}}, "settings": {"published": true}, "properties": {"navigation_color": {"type": "text", "data": "blue"}}}. Pass the object directly — a JSON-encoded string is rejected. wysiwyg/HTML values with embedded quotes are the #1 cause of parse errors when the object is re-stringified.

targetGroupId.description: Optional. Personalization target-group id (from list_target_groups). When set, editables are written as group-specific variants; `appendEditables` is forced to true; `settings` and `properties` must be empty in the data payload.

candidates.description: Propose custom metadata changes to one or more assets for user approval. Does NOT write — generates diffs for review. Returns {results: [...]} where each success entry has a proposalId and failures carry an error with retryable flag. The review widget is shown to the user automatically once a proposal succeeds; end your turn after a successful proposal.

proposals.description: Array of proposals — pass it directly, never as a string. Each entry: {"id": <assetId>, "metadata": [{name, language, type, data}, ...]}. Use get_asset with format="edit" first to see the exact names, types, and dataFormatHint per metadata entry — copy them verbatim. IMPORTANT: `data` values are LITERAL JSON. For relations write {"id": <int>, "type": "object"|"asset"|"document"} as a literal object, never a JSON-encoded string. Multi-relation fields (type "manyToManyRelation") are ADDITIVE by default: send only the member(s) you want to add and existing relations are preserved (de-duplicated by id+type). To overwrite the whole list instead, set "replace": true on that metadata entry. Example (placeholders in <angle brackets>): [{"id": 42, "metadata": [{"name": "<metadataName>", "language": "", "type": "input", "data": "<literal string value>"}, {"name": "<relationMetadataName>", "language": "", "type": "object", "data": {"id": 7, "type": "object"}}]}].

candidates.description: Propose changes to one or more data objects for user approval. Does NOT write — generates diffs for review. Returns {results: [...]} where each success entry has a proposalId and failures carry an error with retryable flag. For retryable errors, fix the data and call again with only the failed entries. Discover the exact shape per class via get_class_definition (top-level fields and their editableDataFormat) and get_field_schema (objectbricks, classificationstore groups, fieldcollection children). IMPORTANT: values inside `data` are LITERAL JSON. Arrays and objects are written directly — never wrap them in an extra string. Example covering the three highest-confusion shapes (placeholders in <angle brackets> — substitute real names from get_class_definition / get_field_schema): [{"id": 42, "data": {"localizedfields": {"<localizedField>": {"en": "…", "de": "…"}}, "<relationField>": [{"id": 7}], "<fcField>": [{"type": "<FCClass>", "data": {"localizedfields": {"<fcSubField>": {"en": "…"}}}}]}}]. Note: localizedfields nests as {"<fieldName>": {"<locale>": <value>}}, NOT {"<locale>": {"<fieldName>": <value>}}. Pass the array directly — a JSON-encoded string is rejected. Each entry MAY also include `removeProposedFields: ["<dotpath>", ...]` — fields to DROP from the proposal entirely (applied after merge with prior pending/refined proposals). Dot-paths work for nested keys (e.g. "localizedfields.title.en"). removeProposedFields.description: Single-object shortcut: list of dot-paths to DROP from the proposal entirely (e.g. ["localizedfields.title.en", "locationAddress"]). Pair with `id`. Removes the field from the proposal — it will NOT be touched on the object. Different from sending `""`/`null`/`[]` as a value, which proposes to CLEAR the value. candidates.name: propose_data_object_update
candidates.description: Propose changes to one or more data objects for user approval. Does NOT write — generates diffs for review. Returns {results: [...]} where each success entry has a proposalId and failures carry an error with retryable flag. For retryable errors, fix the data and call again with only the failed entries. For non-retryable errors, report to the user. Use get_data_object with format="edit" first. The review widget is shown to the user automatically once a proposal succeeds; end your turn after a successful proposal.

proposals.description: Array of proposals. Each entry: {"id": <objectId>, "data": {<field changes>}}. Only include fields you want to change. Discover the exact shape per class via get_class_definition (top-level fields and their editableDataFormat) and get_field_schema (objectbricks, classificationstore groups, fieldcollection children). IMPORTANT: values inside `data` are LITERAL JSON. Arrays and objects are written directly — never wrap them in an extra string. Example covering the three highest-confusion shapes (placeholders in <angle brackets> — substitute real names from get_class_definition / get_field_schema): [{"id": 42, "data": {"localizedfields": {"<localizedField>": {"en": "…", "de": "…"}}, "<relationField>": [{"id": 7}], "<fcField>": [{"type": "<FCClass>", "data": {"localizedfields": {"<fcSubField>": {"en": "…"}}}}]}}]. Note: localizedfields nests as {"<fieldName>": {"<locale>": <value>}}, NOT {"<locale>": {"<fieldName>": <value>}}. Pass the array directly — a JSON-encoded string is rejected. Each entry MAY also include `removeProposedFields: ["<dotpath>", ...]` — fields to DROP from the proposal entirely (applied after merge with prior pending/refined proposals). Dot-paths work for nested keys (e.g. "localizedfields.title.en"). CRITICAL on refinement: "do not change X" / "leave X as-is" requires X in `removeProposedFields` — omitting from `data` keeps the prior proposal's value, not the persisted value.

id.description: Single-object shortcut: data object id. Use only when proposing changes for ONE object — the tool auto-wraps {id, data?, removeProposedFields?} into a one-element proposals array. Ignored when `proposals` is provided.

data.description: Single-object shortcut: field-changes object (same shape as an entry's `data`). Pair with `id`. Ignored when `proposals` is provided.

removeProposedFields.description: Single-object shortcut: list of dot-paths to DROP from the proposal entirely (e.g. ["localizedfields.title.en", "locationAddress"]). Pair with `id`. Removes the field from the proposal — it will NOT be touched on the object. Different from sending `""`/`null`/`[]` as a value, which proposes to CLEAR the value. Ignored when `proposals` is provided.

candidates.name: propose_data_object_update
candidates.description: Propose changes to one or more data objects for user approval. Does NOT write — generates diffs for review. Returns {results: [...]} where each success entry has a proposalId and failures carry an error with retryable flag. For retryable errors, fix the data and call again with only the failed entries. For non-retryable errors, report to the user. Use get_data_object with format="edit" first. The review widget is shown to the user automatically once a proposal succeeds; end your turn after a successful proposal.

proposals.description: Array of proposals. Each entry: {"id": <objectId>, "data": {<field changes>}}. Only include fields you want to change. Discover the exact shape per class via get_class_definition (top-level fields and their editableDataFormat) and get_field_schema (objectbricks, classificationstore groups, fieldcollection children). IMPORTANT: values inside `data` are LITERAL JSON. Arrays and objects are written directly — never wrap them in an extra string. Example covering the three highest-confusion shapes (placeholders in <angle brackets> — substitute real names from get_class_definition / get_field_schema): [{"id": 42, "data": {"localizedfields": {"<localizedField>": {"en": "…", "de": "…"}}, "<relationField>": [{"id": 7}], "<fcField>": [{"type": "<FCClass>", "data": {"localizedfields": {"<fcSubField>": {"en": "…"}}}}]}}]. Note: localizedfields nests as {"<fieldName>": {"<locale>": <value>}}, NOT {"<locale>": {"<fieldName>": <value>}}. Pass the array directly — a JSON-encoded string is rejected. Each entry MAY also include `removeProposedFields: ["<dotpath>", ...]` — fields to DROP from the proposal entirely (applied after merge with prior pending/refined proposals). Dot-paths work for nested keys (e.g. "localizedfields.title.en"). CRITICAL on refinement: "do not change X" / "leave X as-is" requires X in `removeProposedFields` — omitting from `data` keeps the prior proposal's value, not the persisted value.

id.description: Single-object shortcut: data object id. Use only when proposing changes for ONE object — the tool auto-wraps {id, data?, removeProposedFields?} into a one-element proposals array. Ignored when `proposals` is provided.

data.description: Single-object shortcut: field-changes object (same shape as an entry's `data`). Pair with `id`. Ignored when `proposals` is provided.

removeProposedFields.description: Single-object shortcut: list of dot-paths to DROP from the proposal entirely (e.g. ["localizedfields.title.en", "locationAddress"]). Pair with `id`. Removes the field from the proposal — it will NOT be touched on the object. Different from sending `""`/`null`/`[]` as a value, which proposes to CLEAR the value. Ignored when `proposals` is provided.

summary.description: Optional one-line caption shown above the proposal review widget (1-3 sentences). When omitted, a neutral caption is generated automatically.

candidates.name: get_queryable_fields
candidates.description: Get all queryable fields for a data object class. Returns each field as {pqlField, type}; pqlField is what the search tool consumes. Use this before writing PQL filters to discover available fields. These pqlField names are for pqlFilter ONLY — to read values with get_data_object, use plain field names from get_class_definition, not these dotted paths.

className.description: The data object class name (e.g. "Car", "Customer").

candidates.name: get_class_definition
candidates.description: Get the field schema for a data object class. Default returns just {name, type} per field — enough to pick fields for get_data_object(fields=[…]) or to construct a write payload for simple types. For localized fields the children listing is preserved as today. Pass justFieldNames=false to get titles, editableDataFormat hints, examples and metadata. For complex fields (objectbricks, fieldcollections, classificationstore, block), use get_field_schema to explore sub-fields, allowed types, groups, and keys.

className.description: Class name (e.g. "Car", "Customer"). Use list_classes to discover available class names.

justFieldNames.description: When true (default), return only {name, type} per field (localized fields keep their children listing). When false, include title, editableDataFormat hints, examples, and metadata — useful when you need labels or write-format hints.

candidates.name: get_data_object
candidates.description: Get one or more data objects by ID. Default format is "preview" (compact, all languages of localized fields). Use format="edit" for the structured shape needed by propose_data_object_update. Pass fields=["name","price"] (plain names, NOT PQL paths or locale suffixes) to narrow the response. Pass languages=["en","de"] to limit localized blocks to specific locales. Use search_data_objects first to find object IDs.

ids.description: Batch parameter — always `ids` (array), never `id`. Data object IDs. Example: [42, 55, 101]. A JSON-encoded string like "[42, 55, 101]" is also accepted.

format.description: Output format: "preview" (default, compact summaries) or "edit" (structured setter-compatible data for propose_data_object_update).

fields.description: Optional. Plain field names to include, e.g. ["name","price"]. A name matches a top-level field AND any same-named child of localizedFields (one name returns every locale). Use names exactly as in get_class_definition — NOT PQL paths from get_queryable_fields (e.g. "localizedfields.en.name") and NOT locale suffixes (e.g. "name.en"); those decorated forms are coerced when unambiguous, otherwise reported in unknownFields with the valid names. Default: all fields.

languages.description: Optional. Restrict every localizedFields block to just these locales (e.g. ["en","de"]). Default: all valid languages.

candidates.name: update_document
candidates.description: Update editables, settings, and/or properties on an existing document. Editable values can be passed in bare form (just the data — type inferred from the document or template schema) or wrapped form ({"type": "...", "data": ...}). Partial updates preserve other editables (appendEditables defaults to true). Pre-flights validation; on validation failure no save happens. After successful save, post-renders the document and returns any frontend errors in `renderErrors[]` — if non-empty, the document was saved BUT renders broken; pick different element ids/values and call update_document again to fix.For schema and current state, call get_document_schema and get_document first.

data.description: Object with optional keys: editables, settings, properties, appendEditables. Example: {"editables": {"headline": "New title", "cImage_3": {"id": 341}}, "settings": {"published": true}, "properties": {"navigation_color": {"type": "text", "data": "blue"}}}. Pass the object directly — a JSON-encoded string is rejected. wysiwyg/HTML values with embedded quotes are the #1 cause of parse errors when the object is re-stringified.

targetGroupId.description: Optional. Personalization target-group id (from list_target_groups). When set, editables are written as group-specific variants; `appendEditables` is forced to true; `settings` and `properties` must be empty in the data payload.

See the document-editing skill for response shape, when to opt in, and the target-group workflow.

ids.description: Batch parameter — always `ids` (array), never `id`. Document IDs. Example: [12, 18]. Max 5 per call — document content can be large; batch conservatively. A JSON-encoded string like "[12, 18]" is also accepted.

includeProperties.description: Include document properties. Default false. Opt in when reading or editing properties.

candidates.name: list_classes
candidates.description: List all available Pimcore data object classes. Returns class names, IDs, and field summaries. Use this first to discover what data types exist before searching.

candidates.name: get_class_definition
candidates.description: Get the field schema for a data object class. Default returns just {name, type} per field — enough to pick fields for get_data_object(fields=[…]) or to construct a write payload for simple types. For localized fields the children listing is preserved as today. Pass justFieldNames=false to get titles, editableDataFormat hints, examples and metadata. For complex fields (objectbricks, fieldcollections, classificationstore, block), use get_field_schema to explore sub-fields, allowed types, groups, and keys.

className.description: Class name (e.g. "Car", "Customer"). Use list_classes to discover available class names.

justFieldNames.description: When true (default), return only {name, type} per field (localized fields keep their children listing). When false, include title, editableDataFormat hints, examples, and metadata — useful when you need labels or write-format hints.

candidates.name: update_data_object
candidates.description: Update field values on an existing data object. Pass a JSON object mapping field names to new values. Use get_class_definition to learn field names and types.

id.description: The data object ID to update.

data.description: JSON object of field values to set. Example: {"name": "Red Car", "color": "red", "price": 25000}. Only include fields you want to change.

candidates.name: propose_data_object_update
candidates.description: Propose changes to one or more data objects for user approval. Does NOT write — generates diffs for review. Returns {results: [...]} where each success entry has a proposalId and failures carry an error with retryable flag. For retryable errors, fix the data and call again with only the failed entries. For non-retryable errors, report to the user. Use get_data_object with format="edit" first. The review widget is shown to the user automatically once a proposal succeeds; end your turn after a successful proposal.

proposals.description: Array of proposals. Each entry: {"id": <objectId>, "data": {<field changes>}}. Only include fields you want to change. Discover the exact shape per class via get_class_definition (top-level fields and their editableDataFormat) and get_field_schema (objectbricks, classificationstore groups, fieldcollection children). IMPORTANT: values inside `data` are LITERAL JSON. Arrays and objects are written directly — never wrap them in an extra string. Example covering the three highest-confusion shapes (placeholders in <angle brackets> — substitute real names from get_class_definition / get_field_schema): [{"id": 42, "data": {"localizedfields": {"<localizedField>": {"en": "…", "de": "…"}}, "<relationField>": [{"id": 7}], "<fcField>": [{"type": "<FCClass>", "data": {"localizedfields": {"<fcSubField>": {"en": "…"}}}}]}}]. Note: localizedfields nests as {"<fieldName>": {"<locale>": <value>}}, NOT {"<locale>": {"<fieldName>": <value>}}. Pass the array directly — a JSON-encoded string is rejected. Each entry MAY also include `removeProposedFields: ["<dotpath>", ...]` — fields to DROP from the proposal entirely (applied after merge with prior pending/refined proposals). Dot-paths work for nested keys (e.g. "localizedfields.title.en"). CRITICAL on refinement: "do not change X" / "leave X as-is" requires X in `removeProposedFields` — omitting from `data` keeps the prior proposal's value, not the persisted value.

id.description: Single-object shortcut: data object id. Use only when proposing changes for ONE object — the tool auto-wraps {id, data?, removeProposedFields?} into a one-element proposals array. Ignored when `proposals` is provided.

data.description: Single-object shortcut: field-changes object (same shape as an entry's `data`). Pair with `id`. Ignored when `proposals` is provided.

removeProposedFields.description: Single-object shortcut: list of dot-paths to DROP from the proposal entirely (e.g. ["localizedfields.title.en", "locationAddress"]). Pair with `id`. Removes the field from the proposal — it will NOT be touched on the object. Different from sending `""`/`null`/`[]` as a value, which proposes to CLEAR the value. Ignored when `proposals` is provided.

summary.description: Optional one-line caption shown above the proposal review widget (1-3 sentences). When omitted, a neutral caption is generated automatically.

candidates.name: get_data_object
candidates.description: Get one or more data objects by ID. Default format is "preview" (compact, all languages of localized fields). Use format="edit" for the structured shape needed by propose_data_object_update. Pass fields=["name","price"] (plain names, NOT PQL paths or locale suffixes) to narrow the response. Pass languages=["en","de"] to limit localized blocks to specific locales. Use search_data_objects first to find object IDs.

ids.description: Batch parameter — always `ids` (array), never `id`. Data object IDs. Example: [42, 55, 101]. A JSON-encoded string like "[42, 55, 101]" is also accepted.

format.description: Output format: "preview" (default, compact summaries) or "edit" (structured setter-compatible data for propose_data_object_update).

fields.description: Optional. Plain field names to include, e.g. ["name","price"]. A name matches a top-level field AND any same-named child of localizedFields (one name returns every locale). Use names exactly as in get_class_definition — NOT PQL paths from get_queryable_fields (e.g. "localizedfields.en.name") and NOT locale suffixes (e.g. "name.en"); those decorated forms are coerced when unambiguous, otherwise reported in unknownFields with the valid names. Default: all fields.

languages.description: Optional. Restrict every localizedFields block to just these locales (e.g. ["en","de"]). Default: all valid languages.

candidates.name: propose_data_object_update
candidates.description: Propose changes to one or more data objects for user approval. Does NOT write — generates diffs for review. Returns {results: [...]} where each success entry has a proposalId and failures carry an error with retryable flag. For retryable errors, fix the data and call again with only the failed entries. For non-retryable errors, report to the user. Use get_data_object with format="edit" first. The review widget is shown to the user automatically once a proposal succeeds; end your turn after a successful proposal.

proposals.description: Array of proposals. Each entry: {"id": <objectId>, "data": {<field changes>}}. Only include fields you want to change. Discover the exact shape per class via get_class_definition (top-level fields and their editableDataFormat) and get_field_schema (objectbricks, classificationstore groups, fieldcollection children). IMPORTANT: values inside `data` are LITERAL JSON. Arrays and objects are written directly — never wrap them in an extra string. Example covering the three highest-confusion shapes (placeholders in <angle brackets> — substitute real names from get_class_definition / get_field_schema): [{"id": 42, "data": {"localizedfields": {"<localizedField>": {"en": "…", "de": "…"}}, "<relationField>": [{"id": 7}], "<fcField>": [{"type": "<FCClass>", "data": {"localizedfields": {"<fcSubField>": {"en": "…"}}}}]}}]. Note: localizedfields nests as {"<fieldName>": {"<locale>": <value>}}, NOT {"<locale>": {"<fieldName>": <value>}}. Pass the array directly — a JSON-encoded string is rejected. Each entry MAY also include `removeProposedFields: ["<dotpath>", ...]` — fields to DROP from the proposal entirely (applied after merge with prior pending/refined proposals). Dot-paths work for nested keys (e.g. "localizedfields.title.en"). CRITICAL on refinement: "do not change X" / "leave X as-is" requires X in `removeProposedFields` — omitting from `data` keeps the prior proposal's value, not the persisted value.

id.description: Single-object shortcut: data object id. Use only when proposing changes for ONE object — the tool auto-wraps {id, data?, removeProposedFields?} into a one-element proposals array. Ignored when `proposals` is provided.

data.description: Single-object shortcut: field-changes object (same shape as an entry's `data`). Pair with `id`. Ignored when `proposals` is provided.

removeProposedFields.description: Single-object shortcut: list of dot-paths to DROP from the proposal entirely (e.g. ["localizedfields.title.en", "locationAddress"]). Pair with `id`. Removes the field from the proposal — it will NOT be touched on the object. Different from sending `""`/`null`/`[]` as a value, which proposes to CLEAR the value. Ignored when `proposals` is provided.

Pass the array directly — a JSON-encoded string is rejected. wysiwyg/HTML values with embedded quotes are the #1 cause of parse errors when the array is re-stringified.

When set, editables are written as group-specific variants; `appendEditables` is forced to true; `settings` and `properties` must be empty. Applies ONLY to the single-document shortcut (paired with `id`). Ignored when `proposals` is provided — use per-entry `targetGroupId` in that case.

candidates.name: get_document
candidates.description: Get one or more Pimcore documents. See the document-editing skill for response shape, when to opt in, and the target-group workflow.

ids.description: Batch parameter — always `ids` (array), never `id`. Document IDs. Example: [12, 18]. Max 5 per call — document content can be large; batch conservatively. A JSON-encoded string like "[12, 18]" is also accepted.

includeContent.description: Include the document content (the editable widgets and their current values, areablock entries, blocks, inline-resolved element references). Default false. Opt in when reading or editing content; skip when you only need the spine.

includeSettings.description: Include document settings (title, description, controller, template, prettyUrl). Default false. Opt in when changing those.

includeProperties.description: Include document properties. Default false. Opt in when reading or editing properties.

targetGroupId.description: Optional. Personalization target-group id (from list_target_groups). When set, content is returned for that target group context (existing variants surfaced; missing ones fall back to base with `inherited: true`). Implies `includeContent: true`.

candidates.name: create_document

key.description: Document key (URL slug / filename). Lowercase with hyphens (e.g. "my-new-page"). Must be unique within the parent.

parentId.description: Parent document id (typically a folder). Use search_documents or get_document to find a suitable parent.

type.description: Document type. "page"/"snippet"/"email" have editables; "folder" organizes others; "link"/"hardlink" point elsewhere.

title.description: Page title (used as document title for SEO and navigation; only meaningful for type=page). Empty string by default.

navigationName.description: Navigation name (only meaningful for type=page; stored as a property).

template.description: Twig template (e.g. "content/default.html.twig"). Used when type=page/snippet/email. Leave empty when using docTypeId (the preset supplies the template).

docTypeId.description: docTypeId — id of a preset Document Type. When set, supplies controller+template from the preset. Mutually exclusive with explicit template/controller.

published.description: Whether to publish immediately. Default false — recommended to leave unpublished until populated, then publish via update_document.
